title: Stalingrad: WW2 Tactics 1.6 – new trailer for my mobile real-time tactics game (reworked uniforms, trees, explosions)
author: CROCODILE_XXII
selftext:
Squad-level real-time tactics set around Stalingrad, 1942–43: two campaigns (Wehrmacht and Red Army), 40 missions, pause and give orders while paused. Android, made in Godot 4.

How it was made: I don’t write code. All of it was written by Claude Code (Opus 5.5, and Fable 5.2 for the harder visual work). My messages to the agent are the spec. About ten days of intense sessions took it from concept to a near-complete game; shipping and polish took weeks more.

What worked: the project documentation is the agent’s only memory. Every session starts fresh and reads the docs, so every decision gets written down. And no fix counts until I’ve judged it myself on a real tablet, because the agent’s own tests miss what a player sees.

Art: all units and buildings are low-poly models the agent builds in code. For the 1.6 uniform rework, ChatGPT drew redesigns from the agent’s renders, and the agent modelled to that target. The menu art, icon and trailer end card are made with ChatGPT.

What didn’t work: AI-drawn flat tree crowns looked worse than plain 3D trees, so I dropped them. The new 1.6 trees are 3D leaf clusters the agent built.

Happy to answer questions about the workflow.
